newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK inflation to rebound in 1997 - Bank of East Asia.
newsitem.headline: HK inflation to rebound in 1997 - Bank of East Asia.

text.p: Hong Kong's inflation rate will rebound this year after easing in 1996 as anti-inflationary factors are waning, the Bank of East Asia said on Tuesday.
In a research report, the bank forecast Hong Kong's consumer price index (A) would rise between 6.5 and 7.0 percent in 1997, while real gross domestic product should rise 5.0 percent.
In the first 10 months of 1996, the inflation rate stood at an average 6.0 percent, versus 8.7 percent in 1995, it said.
However, transient factors behind last year's lower rate, notably slower increases in housing rentals, are waning and inflation will therefore moderately rebound, it warned.
With the correction in the housing market now over, rental costs are likely to rise faster this year than last year, the report said.
The bank is not optimsitic about Hong Kong's chances of beating inflation further ahead, it said.

A property supplyy that falls some distance short of demand, and a fixed exchange rate that deprives the government of monetary tools will keep the territory's inflation rate above that of its competitors in the long term, the report said.
